title: Quasi-separated sources and qcqs fibre products of algebraic spaces
statement: Work over $\operatorname{Spec}\mathbf Z$, with schemes [def-pc-scheme] and algebraic spaces [def-trf-algebraic-space] in the universes of [def-weil-size-convention]. Use sheaf fibre products [lem-trf-space-fibre-products-etale-covers]. A space is quasi-compact if it admits a representable surjective etale map from a quasi-compact scheme [def-weil-pbc-quasi-compact-scheme]. A morphism $a:A\to B$ is quasi-compact if $A\times_BC$ is quasi-compact for every quasi-compact algebraic space $C\to B$; it is quasi-separated if its diagonal is quasi-compact. A space is quasi-separated if its structure morphism to $\operatorname{Spec}\mathbf Z$ is quasi-separated. Let $g:U\to V$ be a quasi-separated morphism with $V$ quasi-separated. Then $U$ is quasi-separated. Moreover, if $U,V,W$ are quasi-compact and quasi-separated algebraic spaces and $U\to W$, $V\to W$ are morphisms, then $U\times_WV$ is quasi-compact and quasi-separated.

proof.text: Reconcile the conventions of the existing permanence lemma with those of this item. A quasi-compact scheme atlas gives quasi-compact point space by the last clause of [lem-a1-space-finite-affine-subatlas]; conversely quasi-compact point space gives an affine surjective etale atlas by [lem-sfb-qc-space-affine-etale-atlas]. Suppose $h:E\to F$ satisfies the affine-scheme test and $C\to F$ is a quasi-compact algebraic-space test. Choose an affine surjective etale atlas $T\to C$. Then $E\times_FT$ is quasi-compact by the affine test. Its map to $E\times_FC$ is representable surjective etale by [lem-trf-space-fibre-products-etale-covers], so the induced point map is continuous and surjective by [lem-a1-space-point-open-calculus]. The continuous-surjection clause of [lem-a1-space-finite-affine-subatlas] makes $E\times_FC$ quasi-compact on points, hence it has a quasi-compact atlas by [lem-sfb-qc-space-affine-etale-atlas]. Conversely every affine scheme is a quasi-compact space by [lem-weil-pbc-affine-scheme-qcqs], so the space-test condition implies the affine-test condition. These comparisons apply to relative and absolute diagonals as well.

proof.text: Two elementary consequences of the space-test definition will be used. A pullback $A\times_BB'\to B'$ of a quasi-compact map $A\to B$ is quasi-compact: its pullback by any quasi-compact $C\to B'$ is $A\times_BC$. For quasi-compact $A\to B$ and $B\to D$, and any quasi-compact $C\to D$, first $B\times_DC$ is quasi-compact and then $A\times_B(B\times_DC)\cong A\times_DC$ is quasi-compact. Thus composition preserves quasi-compactness. These identifications follow from the universal property of the sheaf fibre products of [lem-trf-space-fibre-products-etale-covers].

source.place: Tags 03HF (lemma-base-change-quasi-compact) and 03HG (lemma-composition-quasi-compact), omitted proofs, transitivity hints written out.

proof.text: Write $Z=\operatorname{Spec}\mathbf Z$. For the first assertion factor the absolute diagonal as $U\xrightarrow{\Delta_g}U\times_VU\xrightarrow{q}U\times_ZU$. The square with top map $q$, bottom map $\Delta_{V/Z}:V\to V\times_ZV$, and vertical maps induced by $g$ is cartesian: on every test scheme its sections are pairs $(u_1,u_2)$ satisfying $g(u_1)=g(u_2)$. Hence $q$ is quasi-compact by step 2 and the quasi-separatedness of $V$. The map $\Delta_g$ is quasi-compact by hypothesis. Step 2 makes their composite $\Delta_{U/Z}$ quasi-compact, proving that $U$ is quasi-separated.

source.place: Tag 04ZH (lemma-separated-over-separated), part (2), via Tag 03KQ (lemma-composition-separated), diagonal factorization and Tag 03KN (lemma-fibre-product-after-map).

proof.text: For the second assertion write $f:U\to W$ and $v:V\to W$. Apply [lem-sfb-space-qcqs-permanence] to $f$: $U$ is quasi-compact and quasi-separated and $W$ is quasi-separated, so $f$ is quasi-compact and quasi-separated. Step 1 identifies its conventions with ours; in particular $\Delta_f:U\to U\times_WU$ is quasi-compact in the space-test sense.

Put $P=U\times_WV$, an algebraic space by [lem-trf-space-fibre-products-etale-covers], and let $p:P\to V$ be the projection. Step 2 applied to the base change of $f$ makes $p$ quasi-compact. The identity test $V\xrightarrow{1}V$ is allowed because $V$ is quasi-compact; it gives $P\times_VV\cong P$ quasi-compact. Next $\Delta_p:P\to P\times_VP$ is the pullback of $\Delta_f$ along the map $P\times_VP\to U\times_WU$ forgetting the common $V$ coordinate. On test schemes the diagonal condition is precisely $u_1=u_2$ for $((u_1,v),(u_2,v))$. Thus step 2 makes $\Delta_p$ quasi-compact, so $p$ is quasi-separated. Apply the first assertion, proved in step 3, to $p$ and the quasi-separated space $V$. It gives absolute quasi-separatedness of $P$. Together with its quasi-compactness this proves the second assertion.
